title: B1: Config Hygiene, Lazy API Clients, GPU Detection & Static Analysis Cleanliness
description:
## Background & Root Cause
`llm_aided_ocr.py` currently has several foundational configuration, dependency, and static-analysis defects:
1. **Eager Import-Time Client Init (`llm_aided_ocr.py:35-36, 48`):** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` default to `"your-anthropic-api-key"` and `"your-openai-api-key"`, making `if not OPENAI_API_KEY:` (`L310`) always `False`, and `openai_client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY)` (`L48`) executes at module import time even when `USE_LOCAL_LLM = True`.
2. **Dead GPU Detection & Unused Dependencies (`llm_aided_ocr.py:13-28, 53-69`, `requirements.txt`):** `nvgpu` is unmaintained, pulls heavy transitive dependencies, and `is_gpu_available()` is never called anywhere. `langdetect` and `scikit-learn` in `requirements.txt` are completely unused.
3. **Static Analysis & Encoding Defects (`ubs .`):** `ubs .` reports 7 Critical and 9 Warning findings, including missing `encoding="utf-8"` on `open()` (`L667, 676`), root `logging.info/warning/error` calls (`LOG015`), legacy `typing.List/Tuple/Dict` imports (`UP035`), and false-positive `py.debug.sensitive-log` warnings triggered by variables named `*token*` inside `logging` format strings.

## Deliverables
- Add `is_valid_api_key(key: str | None) -> bool` that rejects `None`, empty strings, and `your-*-api-key` placeholders.
- Replace module-level `openai_client = AsyncOpenAI(...)` with lazy `get_openai_client() -> AsyncOpenAI`.
- Replace `nvgpu` in `is_gpu_available()` with `shutil.which("nvidia-smi")` and `subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "-L"], ...)` and call it in `load_model()` to auto-select `n_gpu_layers` when GPU is available vs CPU fallback.
- Clean up `requirements.txt` (remove `nvgpu`, `langdetect`, `scikit-learn`; include `pytest` and `pytest-asyncio` for test execution).
- Use module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` everywhere, specify `encoding="utf-8"` on all `open()` calls, and ensure `ubs .` passes with 0 Critical and 0 Warning issues.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AsyncOpenAI is lazily initialized via get_openai_client() rather than at module import time. 2. Placeholder API keys ('your-openai-api-key', 'your-anthropic-api-key', '') are rejected via is_valid_api_key(). 3. is_gpu_available() uses shutil.which('nvidia-smi') + subprocess check without requiring dead nvgpu package, and is wired into load_model() when USE_GPU is active. 4. requirements.txt removes unused nvgpu, langdetect, and scikit-learn. 5. All open() calls specify encoding='utf-8', module-level logger replaces root logging.* calls, modern Python 3.10+ type annotations replace typing.List/Tuple/Dict, and ubs . reports 0 Critical and 0 Warning issues.
close_reason: Implemented lazy API clients, placeholder key rejection, nvidia-smi GPU detection, cleaned requirements.txt, UTF-8 file I/O, module logger, and verified 0 Critical/0 Warning in ubs.

title: B11: Horizontal Line-Strip Median Deskewing & Multi-Page 300-DPI OCR Preservation
description:
## Background & Root Cause (Brenner Falsifier H4)
Running a discriminative 300-DPI OCR experiment on Pages 1, 10, 14, and 15 of `160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter.pdf` proved that whole-page `cv2.minAreaRect(coords)` in `deskew_image()` falsely rotates upright pages that have indented numbered lists or partial pages by 5-12 degrees, severely degrading Tesseract recognition on Pages 10, 14, and 15.
An ablation study isolated 100% of the degradation to `cv2.minAreaRect` on the full-page foreground point cloud (whereas CLAHE + Otsu without false rotation improved recognition, e.g. fixing `-L-` -> `~L4-` and `"Looks"` -> `"looks"` on Page 14).

## Deliverables
- Replace whole-page `cv2.minAreaRect` in `deskew_image()` with horizontal line-strip contour angle estimation:
  1. Dilate inverted binary foreground horizontally (`cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_RECT, (30, 2))`) to merge characters into horizontal text-line strips.
  2. Filter for genuine text-line contours (`w >= 60`, `4 <= h <= 60`, `w / h >= 3.0`).
  3. Fit a line to each contour via `cv2.fitLine(..., cv2.DIST_L2, 0, 0.01, 0.01)` and compute its angle in degrees `atan2(vy, vx)`.
  4. Require at least 3 detected text lines with tight interquartile range (`IQR <= 3.0` degrees) and rotate by the median angle only when `0.25 <= abs(median_angle) <= max_angle`.
acceptance_criteria: 1. deskew_image() uses horizontal morphological line-strip contours and cv2.fitLine median angle estimation (with IQR consistency guard) instead of global cv2.minAreaRect on the whole-page point cloud. 2. Upright pages with indented lists or uneven bottom margins (specifically Pages 1, 10, 14, and 15 of 160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter.pdf at 300 DPI) are never falsely rotated and produce clean Tesseract OCR output. 3. Genuinely tilted document images (e.g. rotated by 4 degrees) are accurately deskewed back to horizontal.
close_reason: Implemented rotationally-invariant horizontal line-strip contour median skew angle estimation (estimate_skew_angle) with IQR consistency gating in deskew_image(); verified zero false rotations on upright pages 1, 10, 14, 15 at 300 DPI and accurate recovery of +/-3.5 to 4.0 degree synthetic skews.

title: B12: Wire Lexical & Embedding Cosine Similarity into Content Conservation & Quality Assessment
description:
## Background & Root Cause
`OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL` (`llm_aided_ocr.py:61, 1393`) is configured and logged in `main()` and mentioned in `README.md`, but was never wired into any function. Adding deterministic lexical cosine similarity (`compute_lexical_similarity`) alongside optional OpenAI embedding cosine similarity (`compute_embedding_similarity`) connects this dead configuration and strengthens `verify_content_conservation()` and `assess_output_quality()`.
acceptance_criteria: 1. compute_lexical_similarity(original_text, processed_text) computes deterministic word + character-trigram cosine similarity and is included in verify_content_conservation() as lexical_cosine_similarity. 2. compute_embedding_similarity(original_text, processed_text) wires in the previously unused OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL when a valid OpenAI API key is configured, with automatic fallback to compute_lexical_similarity() when offline.
close_reason: Implemented compute_lexical_similarity() (word + char-3-gram cosine similarity) and async compute_embedding_similarity() (using OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL with automatic offline fallback), wired into verify_content_conservation() and assess_output_quality().

title: B2: Cached Offline-Safe Tokenizers, Lossless Sentence Chunking & Safe Prompt Sub-Chunking
description:
## Background & Root Cause (Brenner Hypothesis H3)
Token estimation and chunking in `llm_aided_ocr.py` contain multiple data-loss bugs:
1. **Uncached & Crash-Prone Tokenizer (`L167-175, 207`):** `get_tokenizer()` reloads `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b")` or `"huggyllama/llama-7b"` from HuggingFace on every single call without revision pinning (`bandit B615`), and raises an uncaught `ValueError("Unsupported model: ...")` in `chunk_text()` (`L207`) for any model not starting with `gpt-`, `claude-`, or `llama-` (e.g. `o1`, `o3`, `gemini`, or offline runs).
2. **Empty First Chunk & Unused `split_long_sentence()` (`L205-248`):** In `chunk_text()`, if the very first sentence has `sentence_tokens > max_chunk_tokens`, `chunks.append(current_chunk.strip())` appends `""` (`L215`). Meanwhile, `split_long_sentence()` (`L228-248`) is defined right below `chunk_text()` but is 100% dead code (never called).
3. **Silent 50-Word Deletion in `adjust_overlaps()` (`L250-262`):** When `overlap_tokens + current_tokens > max_chunk_tokens`, `L259` executes `overlap_adjusted = chunks[i].split()[:-overlap_size]`, which **deletes the last 50 words of `chunks[i]`** instead of reducing the overlap prefix from `chunks[i-1]`!
4. **Char-vs-Token Confusion & OpenAI 4096 Clamp (`L314, 465, 502`):** `process_chunk()` passes `max_tokens=len(chunk) + 500` (character count ~8,500) and `generate_completion_from_openai()` clamps `max_tokens` to `4096 - prompt_tokens - TOKEN_BUFFER` (`L314`), ignoring `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS = 12000` (`L43`) and truncating 2,000-token chunks in half.
5. **Prompt-Slicing Instructions Loss (`L275, 317, 357`):** When `prompt_tokens > max_prompt_tokens`, `chunk_text(prompt, ...)` slices the *already-formatted prompt string*, leaving sub-chunks `1..N` with raw OCR text and zero instructions.

## Deliverables
- Cache `get_tokenizer(model_name)` with `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=32)` and provide an offline-safe `tiktoken` (`cl100k_base`) + regex fallback so `estimate_tokens()` never crashes on unknown models or offline environments.
- Wire `split_long_sentence()` into `chunk_text()` and `process_document()`, and guard `if current_chunk.strip():` before appending in `chunk_text()`.
- Rewrite `adjust_overlaps()` so `chunks[i]` is 100% preserved and only the prepended overlap prefix from `chunks[i-1]` is reduced to fit `max_chunk_tokens`.
- Use `estimate_tokens(chunk, model_name)` in `process_chunk()`, respect `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` in `generate_completion_from_openai()`, and add a helper to split oversized prompts while re-wrapping each sub-chunk with task instructions.
acceptance_criteria: 1. get_tokenizer() is cached with @lru_cache, uses pinned revisions for HF AutoTokenizer when requested, and falls back deterministically to tiktoken (cl100k_base) or regex word-piece estimation so unknown models and offline runs never crash. 2. chunk_text() never emits an empty first chunk '' when the first sentence exceeds max_chunk_tokens, and wires in split_long_sentence() to split oversized sentences cleanly. 3. adjust_overlaps() never truncates/deletes the tail of chunks[i] when overlap_tokens + current_tokens > max_chunk_tokens; instead it trims or omits the prepended overlap prefix. 4. process_chunk() computes max_tokens from estimate_tokens(chunk) rather than character count len(chunk). 5. generate_completion_from_openai() uses OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS instead of hardcoded 4096. 6. When a chunk overflows token budget in Claude/OpenAI/Local LLM, sub-chunking splits the content while preserving the task instructions on every sub-chunk.
close_reason: Implemented @lru_cache get_tokenizer with offline-safe fallback, lossless chunk_text + split_long_sentence, non-destructive adjust_overlaps, split_oversized_prompt, and OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS support.

title: B3: High-Signal Document Image Preprocessing (CLAHE + Deskew + Otsu) & Configurable PDF DPI
description:
## Background & Root Cause (Mode 12 Signal Processing Analysis)
1. **Mathematical No-Op Dilation (`llm_aided_ocr.py:404-409`):**
   `preprocess_image()` runs `kernel = np.ones((1, 1), np.uint8)` and `dilation = cv2.dilate(gray, kernel, iterations=1)`. In mathematical morphology, dilating by a $1\times 1$ flat structuring element is the identity operation ($I \oplus B_{1\times 1} = I$)—it changes zero pixels while claiming to preprocess the image.
2. **Hardcoded 200 DPI PDF Conversion (`llm_aided_ocr.py:178-199`):**
   `convert_pdf_to_images()` calls `pdf2image.convert_from_path(pdf_path)` without specifying `dpi`, defaulting to 200 DPI instead of the OCR standard 300 DPI, which degrades Tesseract recognition on small typewriter punctuation and footnotes (causing `-10-` -> `-1O-`, `-11-` -> `-LL-`, `-14-` -> `~Li-`, `-15-` -> `~L5-`).

## Deliverables
- Implement `deskew_image(gray: np.ndarray, max_angle: float = 15.0) -> np.ndarray` using foreground text pixel coordinates (`cv2.minAreaRect` / moments) with safe angle clamping so slightly tilted scans are straightened without risking $90^\circ$ rotation flips.
- Upgrade `preprocess_image(image, deskew: bool = True, binarize: bool = True)` to apply:
  1. Grayscale conversion (`cv2.cvtColor`)
  2. Safe deskewing (`deskew_image`)
  3. Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (`cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=2.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))`)
  4. Gentle Gaussian denoising + Otsu binarization (`cv2.threshold(..., cv2.THRESH_BINARY + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)`)
- Add configurable `dpi: int = PDF_DPI` (default 300) to `convert_pdf_to_images()`.
acceptance_criteria: 1. preprocess_image() replaces the no-op np.ones((1, 1), np.uint8) dilation with a real document image enhancement pipeline: grayscale conversion, safe deskewing (deskew_image clamped to +-15 degrees), CLAHE contrast normalization, gentle denoising, and Otsu adaptive binarization. 2. convert_pdf_to_images() accepts configurable dpi (defaulting to PDF_DPI=300 from config) and works end-to-end on 160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter.pdf.
close_reason: Implemented deskew_image + CLAHE + Gaussian denoising + Otsu binarization in preprocess_image and configurable dpi=300 in convert_pdf_to_images.

title: B4: Structural Page Header/Page-Number Stripping & Substantive Footnote Preservation
description:
## Background & Root Cause (Brenner Hypothesis H2)
Forensic comparison of `160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter__raw_ocr_output.txt` against `160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter_llm_corrected.md` proved two critical failures:
1. **100% of Warren Buffett's Substantive Footnotes Were Deleted (~250 words lost):**
   - Page 2 (`raw_ocr_output.txt:98-105`): `* My views on the ambiguity of Accounting Principles Board Opinion No. 8...` — DELETED.
   - Page 7 (`raw_ocr_output.txt:417-426`): `* - An interesting example of this occurred in 1965 when American Express had the salad oil loss...` — DELETED.
   - Page 13 (`raw_ocr_output.txt:778-785`): `* I am leaving OUT of this mathematical warmup the final major variable - coverage Status...` — DELETED.
   Root cause: `markdown_prompt` (`L494`) instructs the LLM to *"suppress headers, footers, and page numbers."* Because author footnotes sit at the bottom of pages, the LLM treats them as "footers" and deletes them!
2. **OCR-Garbled Page Numbers Survived:**
   Tesseract misread typewriter page numbers on pages 10, 11, 14, and 15 as `-1O-` (`L557`), `-LL-` (`L617`), `~Li-` (`L803`), and `~L5-` (`L872`).

## Deliverables
- Implement `is_ocr_page_number_line(line: str) -> bool` recognizing standard and OCR-mangled typewriter page numbers (`- 2 -`, `-1O-`, `-LL-`, `~Li-`, `~L5-`, `Page 12:`) where `[0-9OILlS]` are substituted inside dashes/tildes.
- Implement `clean_page_artifacts(pages: list[str], suppress_headers_and_page_numbers: bool = True) -> list[str]` and `clean_raw_ocr_text(text: str, suppress_headers_and_page_numbers: bool = True) -> str` to strip `Page N:` wrappers, OCR-mangled page numbers, and repeating running headers while keeping 100% of `*` / `†` author footnotes intact.
- Update `markdown_prompt` (`L488-499`) so it explicitly instructs the LLM: *"NEVER delete substantive author footnotes (such as paragraphs or notes starting with `*`, `†`, or `[1]`); format them cleanly as Markdown footnotes or blockquotes."*
acceptance_criteria: 1. clean_page_artifacts() and clean_raw_ocr_text() deterministically strip OCR-garbled page number lines (including '-2-', '-1O-', '-LL-', '~Li-', '~L5-', and 'Page N:' wrappers) and repeating running headers across pages. 2. Substantive author footnotes (lines starting with '*', '†', '‡', or footnote blocks at the bottom of pages) are 100% preserved across all 16 pages of the Warren Buffett letter. 3. markdown_prompt explicitly distinguishes running page headers/numbers from author footnotes (* ...) so the LLM never deletes footnotes.
close_reason: Implemented is_ocr_page_number_line, clean_page_artifacts, and bottom-of-page footnote relocation across mid-sentence page breaks; updated markdown_prompt.

comments.text: Plan-space refinement: Ensure is_ocr_page_number_line() matches standalone dash/tilde-wrapped OCR page tokens (e.g. -2-, -1O-, -LL-, ~Li-, ~L5-) and Page N: headers while never matching negative percentages (-5%), dollar amounts, or bulleted list items.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Brenner causal discovery verified on raw OCR: The 3 deleted footnotes (Pages 2, 8, 15) and the 1 bisected sentence (Page 13) all occur because bottom-of-page footnotes sit between a mid-sentence line at the bottom of Page N (by about / measure turnover / past record, / there is an) and its continuation at the top of Page N+1 ($70,000 / costs with precision / particularly the recent past / offsetting advantage). Relocating bottom-of-page footnotes past the completed paragraph on Page N+1 heals the split sentence AND prevents the LLM from deleting the footnote!

title: B5: Bounded Async API Concurrency & Exponential Backoff Retries
description:
## Background & Root Cause
1. **Unbounded Concurrency (`llm_aided_ocr.py:526-527`):** `process_chunks()` fires `asyncio.gather(*tasks)` across all document chunks simultaneously without a semaphore, triggering HTTP 429 rate-limit errors on multi-page PDFs.
2. **Zero Retry Logic (`llm_aided_ocr.py:266-349`):** Any single transient `APIError` or `RateLimitError` causes `generate_completion_from_claude()` or `generate_completion_from_openai()` to immediately return `None`, which silently drops or un-corrects that chunk in `process_chunk()`.

## Deliverables
- Add `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = config("MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS", default=4, cast=int)` and guard concurrent tasks in `process_chunks()` with `asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS)`.
- Add `retry_with_backoff(coro_factory, max_retries=3, base_delay=1.0)` with exponential backoff and jitter for OpenAI and Anthropic calls.
acceptance_criteria: 1. process_chunks() uses asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS) to bound concurrent API calls. 2. OpenAI and Anthropic completion callers use retry_with_backoff() with exponential backoff and jitter on transient/rate-limit errors.
close_reason: Implemented asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS) in process_chunks and retry_with_backoff with exponential backoff + jitter.

title: B6: Local LLM Model Singleton Cache, Async Thread Offloading & Grammar Fix
description:
## Background & Root Cause
The local LLM execution path (`USE_LOCAL_LLM = True`) in `llm_aided_ocr.py` has four major bugs:
1. **Model Reloaded 2× Per Chunk (`L352`):** `generate_completion_from_local_llm()` calls `llm = await load_model(llm_model_selection)` on every single completion call, reloading a multi-gigabyte `.gguf` file from disk twice for every chunk!
2. **Hardcoded 2048 Context Window (`L45, 152, 355`):** `LOCAL_LLM_CONTEXT_SIZE_IN_TOKENS = 2048` is hardcoded (not read from `.env`), causing every 8,000-character chunk (~2,000 tokens) to overflow `max_prompt_tokens = 1548`.
3. **Synchronous Blocking Inside `async def` (`L83, 152, 377`):** `urllib.request.urlretrieve()`, `Llama(...)`, and `llm(...)` block the asyncio event loop.
4. **Broken Grammar Handling (`L372-396`):** `./grammar_files/` does not exist in the repository, and `L396` runs `.encode('unicode_escape').decode()` which double-escapes backslashes and newlines in JSON output.

## Deliverables
- Add `_MODEL_CACHE: dict[tuple[str, int, bool], Any] = {}` and `clear_model_cache()` so `load_model()` loads the GGUF model once and reuses it across chunks.
- Read `LOCAL_LLM_CONTEXT_SIZE_IN_TOKENS = config("LOCAL_LLM_CONTEXT_SIZE_IN_TOKENS", default=4096, cast=int)`.
- Wrap blocking `Llama(...)` construction, `llm(...)` generation, and model downloading in `asyncio.to_thread(...)`.
- Safely guard `LlamaGrammar.from_file()` when `./grammar_files/` is absent and remove the destructive `.encode('unicode_escape').decode()` transform.
acceptance_criteria: 1. load_model() caches loaded Llama instances in _MODEL_CACHE keyed by (model_selection, n_ctx, use_gpu) so models load once per process instead of 2x per chunk. 2. LOCAL_LLM_CONTEXT_SIZE_IN_TOKENS is read from config() (defaulting to 4096) instead of hardcoded 2048. 3. Blocking llama_cpp model loading, inference, and urllib downloads are offloaded via asyncio.to_thread(). 4. Grammar file loading checks os.path.exists() before calling LlamaGrammar.from_file(), and JSON grammar mode no longer corrupts output with unicode_escape.
close_reason: Implemented _MODEL_CACHE in load_model, config-backed LOCAL_LLM_CONTEXT_SIZE_IN_TOKENS, asyncio.to_thread offloading, and safe grammar handling.

title: B7: Read-Only Cross-Chunk Context, Deterministic Seam Stitcher & Buffett Sample Repair
description:
## Background & Root Cause (Brenner Hypothesis H1 + Mode 62 Sequence Alignment)
In `llm_aided_ocr.py:571-576`, `process_document()` mutates `chunks[1:]` before calling `process_chunks()`:
```python
for i in range(1, len(chunks)):
    prev_chunk_words = chunks[i - 1].split()[-overlap:]
    chunks[i] = " ".join(prev_chunk_words) + " " + chunks[i]
processed_chunks = await process_chunks(chunks, ...)
final_text = "".join(processed_chunks)
```
And in `process_chunks()` (`L526`):
- API mode passes `prev_context=""` to every chunk (`tasks = [process_chunk_with_context(chunk, "", i) ...]`) and discards `new_context` (`L530`).
- Local mode passes `prev_context` only to Step 1 (`ocr_correction_prompt`, `L457`) and NOT to Step 2 (`markdown_prompt`, `L488`), even though `markdown_prompt` asks the LLM to *"Consider the context (before and after the main chunk) to identify duplicates that span chunk boundaries"*.
- Worse, because the 10 overlap words from `chunks[i-1]` are prepended directly as raw text at the start of `chunks[i]`, Step 2 (`markdown_prompt`) frequently formats that short sentence fragment as a `# Heading`, and `"".join(processed_chunks)` (`L576`) concatenates chunks with no newline!
- This produced **5 visibly corrupted chunk seams** in `160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter_llm_corrected.md`:
  1. Seam 1 (`L46`): `Almost all past investments# the price of 300 motor cars.`
  2. Seam 2 (`L86`): `into the pension fund right from the pocketbook of the# Current Postage Rates`
  3. Seam 3 (`L134`): `prices go into a power dive.)the rates rise sharply, prices go into a power dive.)`
  4. Seam 4 (`L194`): `so far.# Calling Flips Indiscriminately`
  5. Seam 5 (`L239`): `Let's take a forged check stub passive approach to the investments.`

## Deliverables
- Stop prepending `prev_chunk_words` onto `chunks[i]` in `process_document()`.
- In `process_chunks()`, compute `prev_context` for every chunk `i > 0` from the tail of `chunks[i-1]` (working in both parallel API mode and sequential local mode) and pass it into both `ocr_correction_prompt` and `markdown_prompt` inside explicit `<previous_context>...</previous_context>` tags with strict instructions never to repeat `<previous_context>` in the output.
- Implement `stitch_chunks(processed_chunks: list[str], overlap_window: int = 25) -> str`:
  - Uses normalized word-token sequence alignment at each boundary `(chunk[i-1], chunk[i])` to detect and strip any echoed overlap prefix on `chunk[i]`.
  - Strips any `<previous_context>...</previous_context>` tags if an LLM echoed them.
  - Detects spurious `# ` heading markers placed on lowercase/mid-sentence fragments at the start of `chunk[i]` when `chunk[i-1]` ended mid-sentence, and stitches with a space (for mid-sentence continuation) or `\n\n` (for paragraph/heading boundaries).
- Repair all 5 corrupted chunk seams and restore all 3 deleted Warren Buffett footnotes in `160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter_llm_corrected.md`.
acceptance_criteria: 1. process_document() no longer mutates chunks[i] by prepending raw words from chunks[i-1]. 2. process_chunks() passes read-only prev_context (tail of chunks[i-1]) in both API and local modes into both Step 1 (ocr_correction_prompt) and Step 2 (markdown_prompt) inside explicit <previous_context> tags. 3. stitch_chunks() deterministically removes any echoed overlap at chunk boundaries, strips spurious mid-sentence '# ' heading markers on lowercase continuations, and joins chunks with clean paragraph/sentence spacing. 4. All 5 corrupted chunk seams (L46, L86, L134, L194, L239) and all 3 missing author footnotes in 160301289-Warren-Buffett-Katharine-Graham-Letter_llm_corrected.md are repaired and verified.
close_reason: Implemented read-only <previous_context> in Step 1 & Step 2, deterministic stitch_chunks seam deduplicator, and repaired all 5 seams + 3 missing footnotes in Buffett sample.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Plan-space refinement: stitch_chunks() must handle both direct prefix-suffix word overlap AND shifted suffix echoes within the first 20 words of chunk[i] (such as Seam 3: prices go into a power dive.)the rates rise sharply, prices go into a power dive.)), plus strip spurious # headings when chunk[i-1] ends with an incomplete clause/preposition (of the, investments) or when the heading starts with a lowercase word.

title: B8: Deterministic Conservation Verifier & Multi-Sample Quality Assessment
description:
## Background & Root Cause (Mode 64 Conservation Laws)
1. **Unaligned Prefix-Only Sampling (`llm_aided_ocr.py:585`):** `assess_output_quality()` only slices `original_text[:max_chars // 2]` and `processed_text[:max_chars // 2]`, completely missing truncation, dropped footnotes, or corrupted seams in the second half of a document.
2. **Broken Multi-Line Explanation Parsing (`llm_aided_ocr.py:625`):** `[line for line in lines if line.startswith('EXPLANATION:')][0]` drops lines 2+ of any multi-line explanation.
3. **No Deterministic Conservation Checks:** An LLM self-grading its own output is non-deterministic. Checking whether numbers (`$10.6 million`, `5%`, `1974`), footnotes (`* ...`), and document length were conserved is 100% deterministic and fast.

## Deliverables
- Implement `verify_content_conservation(original_text: str, processed_text: str) -> dict[str, Any]` returning:
  - `numeric_recall` (fraction of numbers/years/percentages/dollar values from raw OCR preserved in processed Markdown)
  - `missing_numbers` (list of any dropped numbers, excluding stripped page numbers)
  - `footnote_recall` (fraction of substantive footnotes preserved)
  - `seam_anomalies` (list of any mid-sentence `# ` or duplicated seam patterns)
  - `word_retention_ratio` (processed word count / cleaned raw word count)
  - `deterministic_score` (0–100 score based on conservation invariants)
- Upgrade `assess_output_quality()` to sample start, middle, and end windows, fix `EXPLANATION:` parsing with `re.search(r"EXPLANATION:\s*(.*)", response, re.DOTALL)`, and combine LLM quality scoring with `verify_content_conservation()`.
acceptance_criteria: 1. verify_content_conservation(original_text, processed_text) computes deterministic conservation metrics: numeric/currency/percentage token recall, footnote preservation rate, seam integrity check (no mid-word '# ' joins), and word-count ratio. 2. assess_output_quality() samples start, middle, and end segments (instead of only [:7500]), parses multi-line EXPLANATION blocks via re.DOTALL, and integrates verify_content_conservation() so quality assessment works even when an LLM API is unavailable or returns malformed output.
close_reason: Implemented verify_content_conservation and upgraded assess_output_quality with start/mid/end sampling and multiline EXPLANATION regex.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Plan-space refinement: verify_content_conservation() should clean page numbers from original_text before extracting numeric tokens and normalize thousands commas so stripped page numbers and comma formatting differences do not create false conservation penalties.

title: B9: Full-Featured CLI, Docker Build Fixes & README Synchronization
description:
## Background & Root Cause
1. **Minimal Wrapper CLI (`llm-aided-ocr-cli.py:1-27`):** Only accepts a single PDF argument, ignores `.env` overrides from CLI flags, cannot process an existing `__raw_ocr_output.txt` file or run a standalone conservation verification report, and isn't documented in `README.md`.
2. **Broken Docker Build (`docker/Dockerfile:42, 84` & `docker/docker-compose.yml:17`):**
   - `Dockerfile:42` runs `cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` unconditionally (fails when no SSH key exists in build context).
   - `Dockerfile:84` runs `git checkout ${BRANCH}` *before* `cd llm_aided_ocr` (`L85`), failing because `/usr/src/app` is not a git repo.
   - `Dockerfile` omits `poppler-utils`, which `pdf2image` requires at runtime.
   - `docker-compose.yml:17` sets `count: "all"` (string instead of `all`) and mounts Swiss Army Llama files (`models_url.json`).

## Deliverables
- Enhance `llm-aided-ocr-cli.py` with `argparse` options: positional/optional `input_path`, `--raw-ocr-input`, `--output-dir`, `--dpi`, `--provider` (`local`, `openai`, `claude`), `--model`, `--no-preprocess`, `--no-quality-check`, and `--verify-only <raw_ocr> <processed_md>`.
- Fix `docker/Dockerfile` and `docker/docker-compose.yml`.
- Update `README.md` with accurate CLI usage, configuration variables, and architecture documentation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. llm-aided-ocr-cli.py remains backward-compatible with positional PDF path while supporting --raw-ocr-input, --output-dir, --dpi, --provider (local/openai/claude), --model, --no-preprocess, and --verify-only. 2. docker/Dockerfile installs poppler-utils, guards SSH key setup when /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub is absent, and runs git checkout inside llm_aided_ocr/. 3. docker/docker-compose.yml uses count: all (valid integer/all) and LLM_AIDED_OCR env vars instead of Swiss Army Llama leftovers. 4. README.md documents CLI usage, flags, and conservation verification.
close_reason: Upgraded llm-aided-ocr-cli.py with --raw-ocr-input, --output-dir, --dpi, --provider, --model, --verify-only; fixed docker/Dockerfile and docker/docker-compose.yml; updated README.md.

title: B17: Preserve Form-Feed Page Boundaries in Raw OCR Output & Wire Paragraph-Safe Chunking
description:
## Problem
1. In `main()`, `raw_ocr_output = "\n".join(list_of_extracted_text_strings)` strips form-feed (`\x0c`) page boundaries when saving `{base_name}__raw_ocr_output.txt`, causing downstream `clean_raw_ocr_text()` and `--raw-ocr-input` runs to lose multi-page boundary information needed for repeating-header detection and cross-page footnote relocation.
2. `process_document()` contains an inline nested paragraph/sentence loop that mixes split sentences and subsequent paragraphs into `current_chunk` and joins them with `"\n\n"`, turning individual sentences into separate paragraphs instead of delegating oversized paragraphs to `chunk_text()`.

## Action
- Join `list_of_extracted_text_strings` with `"\x0c\n"` in `main()`.
- Extract `split_document_into_chunks(full_text, chunk_size, model_name)` and wire `chunk_text()` for oversized paragraphs so paragraph boundaries are never corrupted.
close_reason: Implemented split_document_into_chunks + form-feed page boundary preservation, reflow_and_dehyphenate_ocr_text + --no-llm CLI mode, and OCR comma-decimal / 96->% numeric conservation normalization

title: B19: OCR-Aware Numeric Conservation (Comma-Decimals & Percent-Sign '96' Confusions)
description:
## Problem
On the flagship Warren Buffett sample, `verify_content_conservation()` reports `missing_numbers: ['28', '496']` (`numeric_recall = 0.9661`) because:
1. Raw OCR has `+2,8%` (comma misread for decimal point in `+2.8%`), which `_extract_significant_numbers()` stripped to `'28'`.
2. Raw OCR has `496 instead of 9%` (`4%` misread by Tesseract as `496`), which was rightly corrected to `4%` in the Markdown.

## Action
- Normalize comma-decimals (`\b(\d+),(\d{1,2})\b` where fractional part is 1-2 digits) to `\1.\2` in `_extract_significant_numbers()`.
- Recognize raw `<prefix>96` tokens repaired to `<prefix>%` in `verify_content_conservation()` so fixing OCR errors is rewarded rather than penalized.
close_reason: Implemented split_document_into_chunks + form-feed page boundary preservation, reflow_and_dehyphenate_ocr_text + --no-llm CLI mode, and OCR comma-decimal / 96->% numeric conservation normalization

title: B18: Deterministic OCR De-Hyphenation & Reflow Engine + Offline --no-llm Pipeline Mode
description:
## Problem
When LLM completion is unavailable (missing API key / network error) or when a user wants fast offline OCR cleanup without an LLM, `process_chunk()` falls back to raw un-reflowed OCR text containing typewriter line-wrap hyphenations (`manage-\nment`) and hard mid-sentence line wraps.

## Action
- Implement `reflow_and_dehyphenate_ocr_text(text: str, reformat_as_markdown: bool = True) -> str` to deterministically repair lowercase line-wrap hyphenations, reflow intra-paragraph hard line wraps while preserving headings/lists/tables, and format author footnotes (`> * ...`).
- Wire `reflow_and_dehyphenate_ocr_text()` into `process_chunk()` as the automatic fallback when `generate_completion()` returns `None`, and expose `--no-llm` in `llm-aided-ocr-cli.py` / `main(use_llm: bool = True)`.
close_reason: Implemented split_document_into_chunks + form-feed page boundary preservation, reflow_and_dehyphenate_ocr_text + --no-llm CLI mode, and OCR comma-decimal / 96->% numeric conservation normalization

title: B16: Guard Lazy API Clients Against Placeholder Keys & Respect Existing Local GGUF Models
description:
## Problem
1. `get_openai_client()` and `get_anthropic_client()` instantiate `AsyncOpenAI` / `AsyncAnthropic` even when the configured API key is a placeholder (`your-openai-api-key`). Consequently, `compute_embedding_similarity()` (called by `assess_output_quality()`) receives a non-None client and attempts live HTTP requests to `api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` with an invalid placeholder key before falling back.
2. `download_models()` ignores `DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL_NAME` and unconditionally checks/downloads the hardcoded default URL even if the user configured a custom local GGUF model that already exists in `./models/`.

## Action
- Make `get_openai_client()` and `get_anthropic_client()` return `None` when `not is_valid_api_key(resolved_key)`.
- Update `download_models(model_name: str | None = None)` to check for existing matching model files in `./models/` using `DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL_NAME` before attempting any download.
close_reason: Guarded get_openai_client() and get_anthropic_client() with is_valid_api_key() so placeholder keys return None without instantiating clients or making bogus network calls, and updated download_models() to check DEFAULT_LOCAL_MODEL_NAME in ./models/ before downloading.
